symbols.name: quantum mechanics
symbols.description: Study and theory of matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

symbols.name: classical physics
symbols.description: Physics describing matter and energy at scales familiar from human experience.

symbols.name: quantum revolution
symbols.description: The shift from classical physical models to quantum mechanics prompted by phenomena classical physics could not explain.

symbols.name: uncertainty principle
symbols.description: Principle that certain properties, such as position and momentum, cannot be simultaneously measured or defined to arbitrary precision.

symbols.name: quantum entanglement
symbols.description: Condition in which the quantum state of particles cannot be described independently, including when they are widely separated.

symbols.name: superfluidity
symbols.description: Quantum phenomenon in which liquid helium near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over its container rim.

symbols.name: black-body radiation
symbols.description: Radiation characterized by a curve of light intensity across frequencies from hot objects.

symbols.name: energy quantum
symbols.description: Discrete unit of energy proposed for light and used to explain black-body radiation and the photoelectric effect.

symbols.name: photon
symbols.description: Quantum or smallest observable particle of the electromagnetic field.

symbols.name: photoelectric effect
symbols.description: Ejection of electrons from a metal surface when illuminated, with electron number depending on light intensity and velocity on frequency.

symbols.name: quantization
symbols.description: Restriction of physical quantities or energies to discrete allowable values.

symbols.name: Rydberg formula
symbols.description: Formula predicting the distinctive absorption-line frequencies of hydrogen gas.

symbols.name: electron
symbols.description: Corpuscular particle whose properties and behavior are central to the quantum phenomena described.

symbols.name: atom
symbols.description: Matter structure whose internal electrons, energy levels, and spectra are modeled by quantum mechanics.

symbols.name: correspondence principle
symbols.description: Requirement that quantum theory converge to classical limits at macroscopic scales.

symbols.name: spin
symbols.description: Quantum degree of freedom associated with electrons and discrete magnetic behavior of atoms.

symbols.name: Stern–Gerlach experiment
symbols.description: Experiment in which a beam of atoms separates into two streams in a magnetic field, demonstrating quantized spin states.

symbols.name: wave function
symbols.description: Quantum description of a system's probabilistic or potential state.

symbols.name: wave function collapse
symbols.description: Conversion of a probabilistic quantum state into a definite measured value through measurement.

symbols.name: eigenstate
symbols.description: State in which an object has a definite value for a specified property or measurement.

symbols.name: eigenvalue
symbols.description: Definite value associated with an eigenstate of a quantum property.

symbols.name: Pauli exclusion principle
symbols.description: Principle that two electrons in an atom cannot have the same set of quantum numbers.

symbols.name: wave–particle duality
symbols.description: Principle that photons and matter exhibit both wave-like and particle-like behavior, neither classical description being sufficient alone.

symbols.name: principle of complementarity
symbols.description: Principle that a quantum system displays wave-like or particle-like properties according to the measurement performed.

symbols.name: double-slit experiment
symbols.description: Experiment in which particles or waves passing through two slits produce an interference pattern.

symbols.name: interference pattern
symbols.description: Pattern of alternating light and dark bands produced by wave interference and reproduced by quantum particles statistically.

symbols.name: Dirac wave equation
symbols.description: Relativistic wave equation for electrons that incorporates relativity and predicts antimatter.

symbols.name: quantum field theory
symbols.description: Quantum theory of fields that permits particle creation and annihilation.

symbols.name: quantum electrodynamics
symbols.description: Quantum field theory of the electromagnetic force.
aliases: quantum theory of the electromagnetic force

symbols.name: quantum field
symbols.description: Field treated within quantum theory, including the electromagnetic field whose quantum is the photon.

symbols.name: quantum tunneling
symbols.description: Quantum process allowing electrons to penetrate a potential barrier.

symbols.name: Standard Model
symbols.description: Quantum field theory describing three fundamental forces and classifying known elementary particles.

symbols.name: Bell inequality
symbols.description: Mathematical constraint on correlations implied by local hidden-variable theories.

symbols.name: local hidden-variable theory
symbols.description: Theory in which measurement outcomes depend on hidden variables local to each separated particle.

symbols.name: Copenhagen interpretation
symbols.description: Interpretation stating that before measurement, statements about a particle's properties are completely meaningless.

symbols.name: many-worlds interpretation
symbols.description: Interpretation describing a multiverse containing every possible universe.

symbols.name: laser
symbols.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

symbols.name: transistor
symbols.description: Quantum-mechanical technological component used in modern electronics.

symbols.name: electron microscope
symbols.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

symbols.name: magnetic resonance imaging
symbols.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

symbols.name: superconductor
symbols.description: Macroscopic quantum phenomenon and technological application of quantum mechanics.

aliases: quantum theory of the electromagnetic force
